Maria Chen: Quick sync — prototyping a "top-swap" canary flow that layers safety checks (probe, quality, drift, budget). want feedback on interfaces and tradeoffs. :thinking:
Kevin Patel: high level — what are Q-layers?
Maria Chen: short: 1) Probe layer (canary health/liveness checks), 2) Quality layer (evals on holdout prompts), 3) Drift detector (statistical divergence vs baseline), 4) Budget/capacity layer (token budgets + latency SLOs).
Sam Rao: curious about latency tax — extra checks add RTT. we should async where possible.
Lina Gomez: agree. runtime should expose lightweight sync probes + async quality hooks. propose endpoints: `/probe` (fast), `/metrics/agg` (batch), `/eval/submit` (async). rollout controller uses `/probe` for fast gating, subscribes to metrics for quality decisions.
Maria Chen: here's a tiny policy example we tested:```yaml
canary_policy:
  probe_window: 30s
  metric_thresholds:
    p50_latency_ms: 150
    rerank_accuracy_drop_pct: 2
  fallback_sequence: [degrade, swap, rollback]
  budget: 50000_tokens/day
```
Kevin Patel: fallback_sequence ordering matters. degrade (lower model size / quantize) before swap so we avoid cache churn. but degrade may change semantics — tradeoff.
Sam Rao: cache/warmup note — swapping to variant will miss KV-cache; warmup cost can spike tail latency. recommend optional warmup mirroring for a small % of traffic: mirror 5-10% to prefill caches.
Lina Gomez: +1. also recommend a TTL-based soft-handoff: route small sticky cohort with extended warmup, then expand. implement as rollout-controller config: `warmup_cohort_size`, `sticky_window`.
Maria Chen: telemetry gating: quality layer should compare nll/perplexity and a small eval set pass rate. define drift as KL>0.07 or per-token deltas beyond 3 sigma.
Kevin Patel: metrics aggregation cadence — per-tenant vs global? per-tenant is noisy but safer. propose hierarchical approach: detect at tenant, escalate to global if many tenants show trend.
Sam Rao: ops implications — need clear abort signals for oncall. ops-bot: "alert: canary_quality_failed (canary_id=top-swap-7) rate=6% over 10m".
Lina Gomez: fallbacks: 1) instant traffic shift to baseline model (fast), 2) transparent degrade (model config change), 3) staged rollback (canary disabled and traffic rebalanced). make sure rollbacks are idempotent.
Maria Chen: interface boundary thought: rollout controller owns policy + decision, runtime exposes minimal control plane (probe/metrics/evict/swap). avoid mixing decision logic in runtime; keep runtime dumb.
Kevin Patel: security/tenant isolation — ensure per-tenant budgets and quotas enforced server-side. rollout controller should pass signed intent tokens to runtime when swapping.
Sam Rao: testing plan — small chaos experiments: drop probe endpoint, simulate drift on eval set, flood warmup traffic. schedule next week?
Lina Gomez: I'll spin up test harness and add canary scenarios to autotests.
Maria Chen: sounds good. action items: Lina => harness, Sam => chaos schedule, Kevin => review escape-hatch UX in console, Ops => ensure alert mapping.
Sam Rao: I'll put a calendar invite.
Maria Chen: thanks all :thumbsup:
